geometry_edits.rationale: Replace generic setback articulation with a more intentional stepped mass operator to improve sectional continuity and terrace legibility.
Orient the stepping along the long axis so the section reads as one continuous landform.
Reduce the number of step events to avoid repetitive tiering and preserve a single dominant gesture.
Tighten the setbacks so the form remains continuous and capacity-bearing rather than fragmented.
Bind the access carve to the verified frontage side so the open space responds to the street edge.
Increase notch width to make the threshold a legible public entry condition.
Extend the notch upward to strengthen a carved void rather than a shallow cut.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent stepped bar in all four views and maintains parcel containment, but the visible mass reads as a generic stacked extrusion with almost no meaningful public void or access-responsive ground condition. The blue frontage edge is not answered by a court, notch, undercut, or entry seam, so the access relation is semantically weak. The silhouette is legible, yet the repetitive tiering feels like code-minimum setback logic rather than an inhabited section or a capacity-bearing landform. For neighborhood living, the form needs a cleaner active threshold and a more carved public figure; as shown, it is more typologically box-like than the program contract wants.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More sculptural and pavilion-like than a neighborhood living bar; roof curvature is not the key transferable element.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part massing with a central void and upper-level connector can create a legible public threshold while keeping the main volume compact.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger and more complex than this candidate; do not copy the tower-perimeter condition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like aggregation around a central court can support neighborhood-scale mixed use if the court is clearly public and the edges stay active.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference leans more retail/market-like and transparent than the candidate; facade openness is not the massing lesson.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated low-rise massing with a central void and horizontal spread is useful for an active ground threshold and calm upper datum.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is more distributed and landscape-integrated; the candidate is too compact and stepped to fully match it.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, spread-out composition can make a public landscape-like void read as part of the section rather than a cutout.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate lacks the clearer void/bridge interplay and reads more like stacked tiers than interlocked program masses.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes with a central courtyard and void-under-block logic can support neighborhood living while preserving hierarchy.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied; the failure is program-semantic and threshold-related, not a site-coverage issue.
The form is coherent across views, so the main problem is not disconnection but insufficient void/public edge logic.
No visible roof or section move meaningfully supports neighborhood-living hierarchy beyond simple stepping.
